source_snapshot.test_name_items: Set LAN source in DHCP via BMC
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set LAN source by:
    - IPMI command - Send command: ipmitool lan set <Channel number> ipsrc dhcp.
    - Web UI - Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Configuration" -> Click "Network" -> Check "Use DHCP".
2. Send command: ipmitool lan print to check LAN information.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: BMC LAN should get an IP address from DHCP server.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 ipsrc dhcp 2>&1; echo ---lan-print---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address Source|MAC Address|IP Address" ; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -i firmware
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: set ch1 LAN source to DHCP then return the FULL `ipmitool lan print` output (IP Address Source, MAC, IP) plus a `mc info` firmware line, so the user confirms the BMC pulled an IP from the DHCP server.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: write to BMC network config (ipsrc dhcp) can drop/re-address the active BMC connection on the managed channel; use a non-management channel and confirm connectivity after.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL chooses a relevant IPMI write and notices disconnection risk, but hard-codes channel 1, exposes credentials with `-P`, assumes the current connection can perform post-write reads and provides no DHCP lease-to-MAC proof, alternate recovery or WebUI coverage.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires channel/interface mapping, isolated DHCP scope, MAC-correlated rediscovery, protected access, backup/rollback and alternate console or management recovery.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 815/2291 retains PARTIAL and the unsafe channel-1 command; it does not validate the post-change address, credential handling, recovery or relationship between the two source control paths.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-980 draft was inspected only as history. This review independently rejects its FULLY AUTOMATABLE class because a management-network write that can sever the agent path requires package/user confirmation under the governing policy.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves source-specified tools while allowing only approved Project alternatives with coverage accounting; ED-36 treats channel, DHCP and recovery artifacts as readiness inputs; ED-38 forbids autonomous connectivity-changing execution and DUT verdicts.

original_test_intent: Verify that the selected BMC LAN interface can be configured for DHCP through the source-specified BMC control path(s), receives a valid DHCP lease belonging to the same physical BMC, reports DHCP source and correct network data, remains recoverably manageable, and can be returned to the approved final configuration.
original_method: Use `ipmitool lan set <Channel number> ipsrc dhcp` and/or the BMC WebUI Configuration > Network > Use DHCP workflow, then inspect the actual mapped channel with `ipmitool lan print`. The source lists both IPMI and WebUI; Project SPEC must state whether they are separate required checkpoints or approved alternatives rather than silently dropping one.
manual_activity: An engineer confirms the chassis, physical management port, channel map, DHCP environment and whether IPMI plus WebUI are both required; maintains alternate/local recovery after the address changes; and restores/validates the final network state. Automation can perform only the approved configuration path and evidence collection after confirmation.
required_inputs: Immutable BMC/chassis identity and mapping among physical port, shared/dedicated mode, IPMI channel, NIC MAC, VLAN and the currently active management connection
Project decision whether IPMI and WebUI are both exercised as separate phases or one is an approved override, with before/restore state for each phase and uncovered method reported
DHCP server/scope/VLAN, reservation or expected policy, client identifier, lease time/window, expected subnet/gateway and authoritative lease-log access
Complete prior static/DHCP network configuration, local host/KCS or serial/alternate-port access that survives the write, rediscovery method and tested rollback/factory-safe recovery
Supported BMC firmware, reviewed internal Script revision, ipmitool/WebUI versions, protected credentials, maintenance window and explicit network-change approval
safety_requirements: Never assume channel 1. Prove the selected channel maps to the intended physical interface and that it is not the sole unrecoverable management path before writing.
Changing `ipsrc` can invalidate the current IP immediately; the recovery observer must not depend on that same session. Establish local KCS/serial or a verified independent path first.
Use an isolated approved DHCP/VLAN environment and correlate the new lease to the recorded BMC MAC/client identity; do not accept any responding address as the target BMC.
Do not expose BMC passwords in argv, logs, screenshots or shell history; use an approved protected authentication mechanism and redact network/credential evidence.
Preserve the complete pre-change configuration and logs. Do not clear evidence, change unrelated channels, guess VLAN/gateway values or retry automatically after loss of access.

If both IPMI and WebUI are required, restore a known baseline between phases so the second method actually performs a transition; do not count two views of one prior change as two control-path validations.

Abort on wrong channel/MAC, unexpected subnet or lease, address conflict, no lease within the approved window, wrong BMC identity, loss of all recovery access or rollback failure. Restore through the independent path before further work.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, inspect supplied mapping, configuration backup, DHCP plan, source-method scope, protected access and independent recovery without changing the BMC.

After approval, execute only the exact Project-authorized IPMI or WebUI path, monitor lease acquisition from the independent observer, rediscover by MAC/client identity and collect post-change channel/network/BMC identity evidence.
If both source paths are required, produce separate baseline-action-lease-readback-restore results and explicitly report any untested method.
Do not select a channel, change the active network, open WebUI, expose credentials, retry after disconnect, improvise recovery or issue DUT PASS/FAIL without the approved plan.
engineer_actions: Approve the channel/port/MAC and DHCP mapping, method coverage, protected access, change window, independent recovery and final/rollback configuration.
Maintain the nondependent recovery path, supervise address rediscovery and restore the approved network state if automation loses reachability.
Confirm physical/network identity, both required method checkpoints and final manageability, then issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lan set <channel> ipsrc dhcp` matches the IPMI source path and `lan print` is useful readback, but hard-coded channel 1, repeated reads to the old IP, `-P` secrets and grep-truncated evidence are unsafe/incomplete; `mc info` does not prove DHCP lease ownership.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Keep the source placeholder `ipmitool lan set <approved-channel> ipsrc dhcp` only after mapping/approval, using protected authentication or local KCS as approved. Rediscover from DHCP lease logs by MAC and collect full mapped-channel readback from the recovered verified BMC; test WebUI separately if required.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: IPMI and WebUI source paths, `<Channel number>` placeholder, `lan print`, Script URL and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot the complete mapped interface; establish independent recovery; execute one approved source path; observe DHCP exchange/lease by MAC; rediscover and verify BMC identity plus full network readback; test the second path from a restored baseline if required; restore the approved final state and confirm management continuity.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC firmware, channel/port topology, shared/dedicated NIC mode, VLAN and DHCP infrastructure.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, NIC/CPLD, WebUI, ipmitool, DHCP server and internal Script commit/version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform IPMI channel map, BMC network/WebUI specification, DHCP policy and Project override approval.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity-safe lease proof, nondependent recovery, secure authentication, per-method coverage and rollback while preserving the source tools.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Testing only IPMI does not validate WebUI control, and vice versa, unless Project engineering approves equivalent coverage; `lan print` alone does not prove the lease came from the intended server or belongs to the same hardware.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Mapped channel, method scope, DHCP identity, backup, recovery, protected access and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A correct DHCP write may still strand the BMC if the lease is unknown, on the wrong VLAN, conflicts, or cannot be reached from the management network.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may approve IPMI, WebUI or another supported BMC network API, but must retain the original paths in the record, state which were actually exercised, document equivalence and leave any untested original interface as a coverage gap.
expected_evidence: Approved chassis/BMC/port/channel/MAC/VLAN map, method-coverage decision, firmware/tool/Script versions and full redacted pre-change network configuration
DHCP scope/reservation/client identity, server-side discovery/request/ack or lease record correlated to the BMC MAC and approved timing
Per tested path: redacted change/audit evidence, session-disconnect timeline, independent recovery/rediscovery and verified BMC identity
Post-change full mapped-channel DHCP source, IP, subnet, gateway, MAC and WebUI state, plus reachability from the intended management domain
Baseline restoration between method phases if applicable, final approved configuration/readback/access, rollback outcome, unexpected logs, coverage gaps and engineer-owned verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: IPMI and WebUI are compatible ways to request the same DHCP state, though the source does not say whether both are mandatory. Project SPEC can define separate checkpoints or an approved override with explicit coverage accounting; no contradictory target or result is present.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target operation and DHCP acceptance are identifiable. Channel, infrastructure, method scope and recovery are execution-readiness inputs; once supplied, the disruptive but reversible test can proceed under confirmation.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps the relevant write/readback concept but removes channel-1, old-IP, credential and truncated-evidence assumptions and adds lease identity plus recovery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation and strengthens the result with explicit two-method coverage, independent-observer requirements and baseline restoration between methods.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Correct OOB placement alone is insufficient; this review proves actual interface and lease identity and plans for the expected disconnect.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects FULLY AUTOMATABLE because connectivity-changing execution requires user confirmation, while retaining its useful capability observation and identity-safe lease correlation.

review_improvement: Prevents a high-risk false success in which channel 1 is changed, the original session disappears and an unrelated DHCP address or stale `lan print` is reported as the tested BMC; it also preserves IPMI-versus-WebUI coverage ownership.
independent_technical_reasoning: DHCP configuration is programmatically controllable, but the write changes the management path on which automation may depend. The test therefore requires confirmed mapping, infrastructure and recovery, not FULLY AUTOMATABLE status. Success is a chain—correct interface write, intended server lease, same BMC identity, usable management and controlled final state—not merely command exit zero.
